To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the dominant source N fueling export changed from nitrate to diazotrophy during the VAHINE experiments, and the δ15N values of surface water dissolved and particulate pools were less responsive to this shift than the sinking particulate pool.

the dominant source for new N to fuel export production shifted from NO3− to N2 fixation in the mesocosm experiments, and that the δ15 N of the surface water PN and DON pools were not responsive to the shift in new N source, while the δ15N signature of PNsink was.
the nitrogen (N) isotope composition of particulate nitrogen (PN) in sinking particles (PNsink) is a sensitive indicator of N sources to surface ocean export production.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the nitrogen cycle in the ocean.
the study of the marine nitrogen cycle, and more specifically, the fate of new nitrogen in the ocean and the role that nitrogen fixation plays in the oceanic nitrogen budget.
the fate of new nitrogen (N) in coastal waters and the factors that control the relative importance of different N sources to export production.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the N source fueling export production in the mesocosm changed from NO3− to N2 fixation during the course of the 23 days.

N2 fixation was not the dominant source of export production during the first 2 weeks of the experiment, but it did become the dominant source by the end of 23 days, with NO3− still supporting export production at a significant rate.
the nitrogen isotopic evidence indicates a shift from nitrite assimilated prior to start of the experiments to nitrogen fixation by the end.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nitrogen isotopic composition of sinking particles in the VAHine mesocosm experiment was controlled by the isotopic composition of the nitrogen pool from which the particles were derived.
we have found a new source of nitrogen for phytoplankton in the oligotrophic ocean.
the N2 fixation was the main source of new N for export in our mesocosm experiments, and that this source became dominant only after about 2 weeks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the isotopic signature of sinking material is a good tracer of the dominant source of newly fixed N to the euphotic zone.
the δ15NSPNsink signal is a useful indicator of the source of new N fueling export, even when the δ15NPNsink signal is not indicative of the dominant source of the N supporting surface production.
the isotopic composition of sinking particulate matter in the surface ocean is a useful tool for inferring changes in the source of new N fueling export.
